name: Religion and Philosophy
description: The great faiths and the great thinkers: from the Vedas, the Buddha and Confucius to Socrates, Jesus, Muhammad, Kant and the philosophers of today.

checkpoints.name: The oldest faiths
checkpoints.note: The Vedas of Hinduism are composed in India, the Hebrew faith in one God takes shape, and Zoroaster teaches in Persia.

checkpoints.name: The age of sages
checkpoints.note: Within a few centuries the Buddha, Mahavira, Confucius and Laozi teach in Asia, and Socrates, Plato and Aristotle in Greece. Their ideas still shape how billions live.

checkpoints.name: Christianity and Islam
checkpoints.note: Jesus teaches in Judea and Christianity spreads through the Roman Empire. Muhammad founds Islam in Arabia, and it spreads from Spain to India within a century.

checkpoints.name: Medieval thought
checkpoints.note: Scholars such as Avicenna, Averroes, Maimonides and Aquinas join faith with Greek philosophy. Sikhism begins in the Punjab.

checkpoints.name: Reform and Enlightenment
checkpoints.note: Luther starts the Reformation. Descartes, Locke, Hume and Kant ask what we can know and how we should be governed.

checkpoints.name: Modern thought and faiths
checkpoints.note: Marx, Nietzsche and the existentialists question old certainties. New faiths and movements appear, and the great religions spread around the world.
